images.caption: Fig. 1:The horizontal and vertical axes indicate the numbers of methods with fake audio and fake visual output, respectively. The size of each circle represents the total dataset size. Circle color encodes the dataset modality, and the color gradient within each modality encodes the year of its latest forgery method. Mega-MMDF covers 12 methods with fake audio output and 20 with fake visual output. The T2AV methods are included in both counts, yielding 30 methods in total. Mega-MMDF contains 1.3 million audio-visual clips across 22 forgery pipelines.

Fig. 9:Selected clip-level fake-probability distributions before and after modality masking on Mega-MMDF. Vertical axes show within-class proportions with panel-specific scales, while horizontal axes show the predicted fake probability. Dotted lines mark the decision threshold of 0.5, and shaded areas indicate the error regions. Audio masking can shift authentic clips toward higher fake probabilities (a), while video masking can increase false alarms on authentic clips (b) and missed detections on clips with forged audio (c–d).
